svg.title: Advanced retrieval as a router
svg.desc: A hand-drawn router diagram. A query enters a small classifier — an LLM call or a rules engine — which branches five ways by the shape of the question. A structured question goes to text-to-SQL with a schema-aware prompt and a read-only execution role. A question needing traversal goes to GraphRAG, which walks the entity graph one or two hops. A question containing a rare exact term goes to late-interaction retrieval, scoring per-token MaxSim over short answer spans. A whole-document question skips retrieval entirely, loads the document, and caches the prefix. Everything else falls through to standard hybrid RAG with a reranker, which carries most of the traffic. A caption notes that getting the routing right often lifts answer quality more than any single technique, because the wrong retriever on the wrong query returns nothing at all.
svg.text: A small classifier reads the shape of each question and dispatches it to the retriever that shape demands.
traverse the entity graph one or two hops
skip retrieval, load it all, cache the prefix
the fall-through, and most of the traffic
Getting the routing right often lifts answer quality more than any single technique does: the wrong retriever on the wrong query returns nothing.
